title: Company Access, Change, and Supplier Playbook
author: Amina Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates company-wide policies and standard procedures for access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor lifecycle management, travel policy, and the canonical internal templates used by cross-functional teams. It is intended as the single operational reference for requesters, approvers, and operational teams.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and contingent workers.
- Covers corporate systems (G Suite, Okta, Redwood Console), infrastructure systems (redwood-iam, cluster-admin, provisioner), procurement and expense approvals, vendor onboarding and offboarding, and employee travel booked on company funds.
- Does NOT replace team-specific technical runbooks; it complements them by defining approval flows, classification, and control gates.

Roles and Responsibilities

- Requester: initiates access/change/procurement/travel requests and provides justification and cost estimates.
- Approver: designated person(s) in the approval matrix (see table) who validate business need, least-privilege fit, and budget.
- Security Owner: reviews data classification implications and authorizes data access for sensitive resources.
- Procurement Owner (Finance): validates vendor contracts, tax documentation, and budget availability.
- IT/Platform: executes approved changes, provisions access, and records artifacts/logs.
- Vendor Manager: manages vendor relationship, renewal, SLAs, and offboarding.

Approval Matrix (summary)

| Item Category | Typical Approver | Additional Approvals Required | Approval SLA |
|---------------|------------------|------------------------------|--------------|
| Standard SaaS user access | Team Lead | None | 48 hours |
| Admin access to production | Engineering Manager + Security Owner | CTO for >30 days | 24 hours |
| Infrastructure change (non-prod) | Service Owner | SRE review for risk > medium | 48 hours |
| Infrastructure change (prod) | SRE Lead + Change Manager | Security + Product if user-facing | 4 hours planned window |
| Procurement < $5k | Requester’s Manager | Finance automated approval | 72 hours |
| Procurement $5k–$50k | Manager + Procurement Owner | Legal review if contract | 10 business days |
| Procurement > $50k | Exec Sponsor + Procurement Owner + Legal | Procurement Committee | 20 business days |

Access and Permissions

Principles
- Least privilege by default.
- Time-bounded elevated access (default 7–90 days depending on role).
- All privileged access must use MFA and recorded session logging (redwood-iam + session-replay).

Standard Procedures
1. Initiate a request via Access Portal (https://internal.redwood/access). Provide: business justification, requested role, resources, and desired duration.
2. Auto-check: portal enforces least-privilege role suggestions using profile templates.
3. Approval step: manager approves; sensitive access triggers Security Owner review.
4. Provisioning: IT/Platform provisions with time-bound expiry and sends user onboarding checklist.
5. Audit: Quarterly entitlement review emails are sent to all managers; remediation within 14 days.

Example CLI (for privileged temporary access):

redwood-iam grant-temporary --user alice@redwood.com --role infra-admin --duration 72h --justification "hotfix for KV cache"

Change Management (technical and non-technical)

Policy Summary
- All production-impacting changes must be scheduled in the Change Calendar and follow the Change Approval process. Emergency changes require post-facto review.
- Changes are grouped into Standard, Normal, and Emergency categories.

Change Process (Normal)
1. Create a change request in Change Tracker with CI/CD link, rollback plan, and blast radius estimation.
2. Run pre-deployment checks: automated integration tests, canary config, and perf smoke test.
3. Obtain approvals: Service Owner -> SRE -> Change Manager -> Security (if sensitive).
4. Schedule in Change Calendar and notify on-call.
5. Execute in the approved window with runbook steps recorded.
6. Post-change validation: health checks, telemetry review, error budget impact assessment.
7. Close-out: write a short change summary in the tracker within 24 hours.

Emergency Change Process
- If an incident requires an immediate fix, the engineer may perform Emergency Change with approval from the on-call SRE and an executive ping (Slack #oncall-exec). The change must be logged and a postmortem/root-cause analysis created within 72 hours.

Change Categorization Table

| Category | Definition | Expected Approval Path |
|----------|------------|------------------------|
| Standard | Repeatable, low-risk with pre-approved checklist | Auto-approved by Change Manager |
| Normal | New change requiring explicit approvals | Service Owner -> SRE -> Change Manager |
| Emergency | Immediate mitigation to stop active incident | On-call SRE -> Exec ping; retrospective required |

Data Management and Classification

Classification Levels
- Public: information intended for unrestricted public release.
- Internal: non-sensitive internal information.
- Confidential: PII, business metrics, or contractual information requiring access control.
- Restricted: regulated data (e.g., GDPR special categories, PCI) requiring encryption at rest and in-transit and explicit data-handling SOPs.

Data Handling Controls
- Confidential/Restricted data stored only in approved storage buckets with KMS keys managed via customer-kms / redwood-kms.
- Export and sharing rules: Confidential cannot be shared to personal email; Restricted requires DLP approval.
- Retention: follow retention schedule documented in Data Retention Matrix (see templates section).

Data Access Request Flow
1. Requester files Data Access Request (DAR) with dataset identifier, reason, and duration.
2. Data Steward validates need and assigns a reviewer.
3. Security Owner assesses environment and approves if controls are adequate.
4. IT provisions scoped access in a sandbox if possible.

Procurement and Expenses

Principles
- Centralize vendor evaluation and contract negotiation for anything material (> $50k).
- Enforce competitive procurement for recurring spend > $25k/year (minimum two bids).
- Use company credit cards only for approved travel and low-value purchases (policy exceptions require an approval ticket).

Procurement Workflow
1. Create a Purchase Request in ProcureFlow with business justification, budget code, and anticipated contract term.
2. Procurement Owner runs vendor risk assessment (security questionnaire, SOC reports, references).
3. Legal reviews contract for indemnity, data residency, and termination clauses.
4. Finance allocates budget and issues PO.
5. Vendor onboarding (see Vendor Management).

Expense Reimbursement
- Employees submit expenses via ExpenseBot within 30 days of purchase with receipts.
- Non-compliant claims are routed back for correction; repeat offenders are reviewed by people-ops.
- Per diem and travel allowance charts are maintained in the Templates section.

Vendor Lifecycle and Management

Onboarding Checklist
- Complete vendor intake form in Vendor Portal.
- Collect W-9 / W-8 (as applicable), SOC2 or audit evidence, security questionnaire, and insurance certificates.
- Confirm data handling requirements and designate a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) if vendor processes personal data.
- Create vendor record in ERP and assign Vendor Manager.

SLA and Risk Monitoring
- Every vendor with access to production or to Confidential/Restricted data must have an SLA and security attestations reviewed annually.
- Vendors are scored on a risk rubric (confidentiality, criticality, financial stability) and audited per schedule based on risk tier.

Offboarding
- Ensure account revocation in all systems, retrieval or deletion of data as contract requires, and confirmation that all company assets are returned.
- Send formal termination notice and archive contract in Contract Vault.

Travel Policy (summary)

Booking and Approvals
- All business travel must be booked using Travel Portal (Concur) and pre-approved by a manager. Out-of-policy bookings may not be reimbursed.
- Preferred vendors must be used for flights and hotels when available.

Spending Guidelines
- Economy class for flights < 8 hours. Business class permitted with Exec Sponsor approval for flights > 8 hours.
- Hotel rates should use the corporate negotiated rate where possible.

Travel Safety and Data
- Employees traveling with devices must enable disk encryption and ensure VPN access.
- Do not store Restricted data on personal devices.

Internal Templates and Forms

Included Templates (canonical locations)
- Access request template: /templates/access-request.md
- Change request template: /templates/change-request.yml
- Vendor intake form: /templates/vendor-intake.xlsx
- Data Retention Matrix: /templates/data-retention.csv
- Expense report template: /templates/expense-template.xlsx

Template Example: change-request.yml\
---
title: "Change Request"
service: "<service-name>"
author: "<your-name>"
change_type: "normal | standard | emergency"
rollback_plan: "|\n  - step1\n  - step2"
impact_area: "<prod|non-prod>"
scheduled_window: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ"
prechecks: "smoke-tests, canary"
post_validation: "metrics: latency, error-rate"
---

Audit, Monitoring and Reporting

- All approvals and provisioning events are logged in the Audit Ledger (immutable). Retention 7 years for procurement and vendor contracts, 3 years for access logs unless tied to security investigations.
- Monthly compliance report aggregates: pending access requests older than SLA, open vendor risks, and change window violations.

Enforcement and Exceptions

- Exceptions require a documented risk acceptance ticket and approval by the relevant business owner and Security Owner. Exceptions are reviewed quarterly.
- Noncompliance triggers remediation plans; repeated violations escalate to people-ops and may affect compensation.

Continuous Improvement

- The playbook is reviewed biannually by Finance, Security, and People-Ops. Suggested updates should be submitted via the Policy Update form. Significant changes require an announcement and a 14-day comment period.

Appendices

A. Quick Contact List
- Change Manager: change-manager@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Vendor Manager: vendor-manager@redwood.com
- Security Owner: security-policy@redwood.com

B. Risk Triage Rubric (summary)
- Low: non-critical SaaS, Internal data only. Review every 24 months.
- Medium: critical SaaS or Confidential data. Review annually.
- High: production-access vendors or Restricted data. Quarterly review and SOC2/PTR evidence required.

C. Common Scenarios (short answers)
- "How do I get read-only access to analytics?" - File Access Request -> Team Lead approves -> Provisioned as read-only for 90 days.
- "Urgent security patch needed outside maintenance window" - Execute Emergency Change with on-call SRE approval and log the change.
